To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) A non parametric classification objective can be used to learn a good feature space that captures apparent similarity between instances, and 2) This feature can be used for various downstream applications, such as classification, semi supervised learning, and object detection.

(i) unsupervised feature learning can be achieved by non parametric instance discrimination, (ii) the learned features are useful for semi supervised learning, object detection, and nearest neighbour search, and (iii) the learned feature representation is compact.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a simple but powerful idea that a feature can be learned without supervision, by merely requiring it to be discriminative at the instance level.
unsupervised feature learning for visual recognition.
the following question: What is the best representation that captures apparent visual similarity among instances?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a new approach to unsupervised learning that is both conceptually simple and empirically effective.
the proposed method is a powerful unsupervised representation learning method, that outperforms the state of the arts on various tasks and settings.
our method is able to learn good features that capture visual similarity at the instance level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can achieve the state of the arts for unsupervised feature learning, semi supervised feature learning, and instance level feature learning.
, with a simple yet elegant objective, we have demonstrated that instance discrimination can be an effective way to achieve unsupervised feature learning.
, by merely learning to discriminate instances, we are able to achieve state of the art performance on various vision tasks, with a compact feature representation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of class labels, a feature can be trained to capture apparent visual similarity by being discriminative of individual images.
, by learning to discriminate individual instances rather than classes, a neural net can capture apparent similarity among instances in an unsupervised manner.
, by learning to discriminate among instances, the feature space can be made more amenable to nearest neighbour retrieval.
